stem: A big block M is on a smooth horizontal floor. A small block A (mass m) sits on top of M and is joined by a light string over a pulley at M's top-right corner to a second small block B (mass m) hanging against M's vertical right face. Friction coefficient between M and both small blocks is μ. Find the maximum horizontal force F applied to M for which the small blocks stay at rest relative to M.
Same three-block stack. Find the minimum value of F for which A slips on B. (a) 125 N (b) 150 N (c) 175 N (d) 180 N

key: a, c T = 500 N; a B = 2 m/s²
stem: Multiple correct. Two blocks A (10 kg) and B (50 kg) are arranged as shown (a 37° surface above them, a string, and a rough vertical wall on the right). Coefficient of friction between all surfaces is 0.5, g = 10 m/s². Which are correct? (a) tension in the string is 500 N (b) tension in the string is 400 N (c) acceleration of block B is 2 m/s² (d) acceleration of block B is 3 m/s².

Same passage (monkey m descending w.r.t. the rope with acceleration b, block M on a table with friction μ). The tension of the rope is (a) Mm(μg+g+b)/(M+m) (b) Mm(μg−g+b)/(M+m) (c) Mm(μg+g−b)/(M+m) (d) Mm(μg−g−b)/(M+m)

A given object takes n times the time to slide down a 45° rough inclined plane as it takes to slide down an identical perfectly smooth 45° inclined plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface of the inclined plane is (a) √(1 − 1/n²) (b) 1 − n² (c) 1 − 1/n² (d) √(1 − n²)

A block of mass 1 kg is pushed up a surface inclined at 60° to the horizontal by a force of 10 N parallel to the inclined surface, with μ s = 0.1. When the block is pushed up by 10 m along the inclined surface, the work done against frictional force is (g = 10 m s⁻²): (a) 5√3 J (b) 5 J (c) 5 × 10³ J (d) 10 J

Consider a block kept on an inclined plane (inclined at 45°). If the force required to just push it up the incline is 2 times the force required to just prevent it from sliding down, the coefficient of friction between the block and inclined plane (μ) is equal to: (a) 0.33 (b) 0.60 (c) 0.25 (d) 0.50

A uniform chain of 6 m length is placed on a table such that a part of its length is hanging over the edge of the table. The system is at rest. The coefficient of static friction between the chain and the surface of the table is 0.5. The maximum length of the chain hanging from the table is ___ m.
